title: Sean Payton turns over play calling to new Broncos OC Davis Webb
content:
INDIANAPOLIS — It turns out the answer to the Denver Broncos’ big offseason question was one of the league’s worst-kept secrets all along.

When Buffalo Bills general manager Brandon Beane met with reporters at the NFL Scouting Combine on Tuesday afternoon, he gave a glowing review of the Broncos’ new offensive coordinator, Davis Webb, who spent three seasons in Buffalo as a backup quarterback. Then, Beane broke some news.

“He’s going to get an opportunity, I believe, to call plays now,” Beane said of Webb, “which I think will only help his resume.”

A few hours later, Broncos coach Sean Payton had his turn at the podium, but not before running into Beane in the hallway.

“I thought, ‘You can come in and do my presser, too,'” Payton said with a grin.

The veteran head coach confirmed he is indeed passing the play-calling baton for the first time in his career as a head coach, which began in New Orleans in 2006. Past coordinators such as Pete Carmichael and Joe Lombardi occasionally called plays during preseason games. Webb himself called Denver’s final exhibition in 2025. Carmichael briefly took over the role during the 2011 regular season after Payton suffered a broken leg in a sideline collision. But this season will mark the first time someone other than Payton will be calling his team’s offense full-time.

It represents a massive change for Payton and the Broncos, who ended their season with a loss in the AFC Championship Game last month.

“I think he’ll be really good at it,” Payton said of Webb, the 31-year-old who was Denver’s quarterbacks coach the past three seasons. “I know that’s like, ‘Man, are you going to give up play calling?’ I would only do that if I felt like it would help our team. I’ll still be involved with what we do offensively, just like I do with what we do defensively, but I do think he has a gift. I think he’s real sharp. I’m glad he’s on our staff. Typically, any decision we make like that is to benefit our team. Listen, I’m looking forward to it.”

Payton said he began pondering the change midway through last season. He met with Webb at the time to discuss how he could have greater input on Denver’s offense and the potential of calling plays at some point in the future. Payton fired Lombardi, his offensive coordinator the past three years in Denver, after the season and promoted Webb into the role after Webb completed a circuit of interviews for head coach openings in Las Vegas and Buffalo and multiple outside offensive coordinator roles.

Webb now will call plays for Bo Nix, the quarterback he has helped develop the last two seasons.

“I think Davis is an absolute stud, he’s going to be great regardless,” new Bills head coach Joe Brady, a former Payton assistant, told reporters at the combine Tuesday. “But to have somebody that’s been through it and has called games at a high level, to pick his brain and everything like that — that’s going to be a huge resource for him.”

Payton said he’ll still call “some plays” on game days and still guide the offensive game-planning process throughout the week. Asked how aggressive he expects Webb to be as a play caller, Payton said that will be dictated by “what the head coach wants.” Still, Payton is loosening his proverbial grip on the offense. It’s a decision that wasn’t dictated by his own performance as a play caller, Payton said, but rather what he believes Webb can inject into an offense that finished 14th in scoring last season and 10th in yards per game.

“The cool thing is he’s one of the best to ever call it, and yet he’s going to let this young up-and-comer (call plays), and that just shows you how much he believes in Davis,” Broncos general manager George Paton said.

Webb has been an NFL coach for only three seasons, a career he began just weeks after starting the 2022 regular-season finale at quarterback for the New York Giants. Really, though, Webb’s coaching journey began far earlier. He was as much a teacher as he was a player during his six NFL seasons with the Giants and Bills.

“We saw the coaching side of Davis as a player,” Beane said Tuesday. “There were many times we would acquire a player in the season and the coaches are up there (in their offices) game-planning, and Davis said — it could be a running back, receiver, tight end — ‘I’ll take him down to the meeting room myself and school him up.’ I know that was one of the reasons Brian Daboll wanted to get him to New York to help him install his offense and teach as many people as he could. He’s a natural teacher and a natural communicator.”

Webb’s promotion to a play-calling offensive coordinator role comes as the Broncos also, to the surprise of many in their building, retained Vance Joseph as defensive coordinator. Joseph, who has guided one of the NFL’s best defenses the past two seasons, had multiple interviews for head coach jobs, but he wasn’t hired to fill any of the 10 vacancies around the league.

“I know he felt like he had a handful of interviews that were productive, which he felt were really good opportunities,” Payton said of Joseph. “I know that when that opportunity comes for him, he’ll be successful. He’s got a presence about him. One of his superpowers is his calming presence and he pulls the best out of his players who play for him. There’s 32 of these teams that are owned individually and every one is different, and yet a lot of them have trouble getting out of their own way.”
